title: Make tutor audit-log writes idempotent and failure-visible instead of best-effort auto-ID writes

evidence.quote: /** Write an audit log entry for a tutor mutation (best-effort — errors are logged but not thrown). */

} catch (e) {
    logger.warn(`writeAuditLog: failed for grant=${grantId} action=${action}`, e);

why: The audit log is the parent's only visibility into what an invited tutor did to their child's data (12-month retention, W3.42), but every write to it is swallowed on failure (the primary mutation still returns success:true even if its audit entry silently failed) and keyed by Firestore auto-ID rather than a deterministic key, so a client-side retry of a timed-out-but-actually-succeeded Cloud Function call produces a duplicate entry for the same real action. A parent reviewing the trail can see gaps or phantom duplicates with no way to tell which from inside the app.
recommendation: Derive a deterministic audit_log doc ID from (grantId, action, target, an idempotency key) so retries coalesce, and consider writing the audit entry in the same batch/transaction as the primary mutation so both succeed or fail together.
acceptance_criteria: Calling the same tutor mutation twice with the same idempotency key produces exactly one audit_log entry, proven by a new test.
